themes.label: Motivation: functional time series and the two-sample problem
themes.need: Someone new to functional time series needs to understand why temporal dependence between curves matters and why a formal two-sample mean-equality test is needed instead of visual comparison.
themes.distributed_justification: Introduction paragraphs interrupted only by an excluded Pass A caption-stub trash span (33-34); same motivation/background need before and after.

themes.label: Weak-dependence condition (L2-m-approximability)
themes.need: Someone choosing a dependence assumption for a functional time series model needs the formal L2-m-approximability condition and what it requires of the generating mechanism.

themes.label: CLT for the sample mean of a dependent functional time series
themes.need: Someone needing a distributional approximation for the sample mean curve of dependent functional data needs the central limit theorem statement and its derivation.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 2.1's statement (Section 2 intro + conditions) and its proof (Section 5) serve one need — the CLT and its derivation — per R7b.

themes.label: Estimating and proving consistency of the long-run covariance kernel
themes.need: Someone needing to quantify the variability of a functional sample mean under dependence needs a consistent estimator of the long-run covariance kernel and proof of its consistency.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 2.2's statement/estimator definition (Section 2) and its proof (Section 5) serve one need — kernel estimation and its consistency — per R7b.

themes.label: Two-sample testing setup
themes.need: Someone setting up a two-sample comparison of dependent functional data needs the location models, the null/alternative hypotheses, and the natural test statistic U_N,M.

themes.label: Null/alternative asymptotics of raw U_N,M
themes.need: Someone wanting to know the asymptotic behavior of the raw two-sample statistic needs its limiting null and alternative distributions and the Karhunen-Loeve representation that makes them computable.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorems 3.1/3.2's statements (Section 3) and their proofs (Section 6, immediately preceded by the shared relations (6.1)) serve one need — the raw statistic's asymptotics — per R7b.

themes.label: Constructing implementable statistics U(1), U(2)
themes.need: Someone implementing the two-sample test needs to know how the practical statistics U(1) and U(2) are built from empirical eigenprojections when the population eigenstructure is unknown.

themes.label: Null distribution of U(1)/U(2)
themes.need: Someone computing a p-value from U(1) or U(2) needs their asymptotic null distributions and the justification that these hold.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 3.3's statement and its proof (Section 6) serve one need — U(1)/U(2)'s null distribution — per R7b.

themes.label: Consistency/power of U(1)/U(2) under the alternative
themes.need: Someone assessing test power needs to know whether and how U(1) and U(2) diverge under a true difference in mean functions.
themes.distributed_justification: Theorem 3.4's statement and its proof (Section 6) serve one need — U(1)/U(2)'s behavior under the alternative — per R7b.

themes.label: Estimating the covariance kernel d(t,s)
themes.need: Someone implementing the test needs a way to estimate the unknown kernel d(t,s) driving U(1)/U(2), both when errors are iid and when they are temporally dependent.

themes.label: Numerical implementation algorithm
themes.need: Someone coding up the test needs the numerical recipe — basis expansion, the reduced matrix eigenproblem, and computing the projections — to actually calculate U(1) and U(2).

themes.label: Simulation study: size and power
themes.need: Someone deciding whether to trust this test on real data needs simulated evidence of its empirical size and power under both independent and temporally dependent functional errors.

themes.label: Medfly application
themes.need: Someone applying the test to an independent-curves setting needs to see whether short-lived and long-lived medflies have significantly different mean egg-laying curves.

themes.label: Eurodollar futures application
themes.need: Someone applying the test to dependent financial curves needs to see whether Eurodollar futures curves from different time periods have significantly different mean functions.
themes.distributed_justification: Eurodollar example (dataset, samples, interpretation, results) interrupted by the general Section 4.4 recap paragraph (b064/b066, excluded as unassigned); Table 4.4 continues the same empirical need.

themes.label: Practical guidance: choosing the statistic and dimension p
themes.need: Someone about to run this test needs practical guidance on which statistic, U(1) vs U(2), to prefer and how many components p to use.
